# Sirach Chapter 34 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_034_page_001.jpg

---

**34:1** Empty and false hopes are for the senseless, and dreams give wings to fools.

**34:2** Like one who catches at a shadow and chases the wind, so is the one who pays attention to dreams.

**34:3** What is seen in dreams is a reflection, the likeness of a face opposite a face.

**34:4** From an unclean thing, what can be cleansed? And from what is false, what can be true?

**34:5** Divinations and auguries and dreams are vain, and the heart imagines fantasies like a woman in labor.

**34:6** Unless they are sent as a visitation from the Most High, do not give your heart to them.

**34:7** For dreams have led many astray, and those who have hoped in them have perished.

**34:8** Without lying, the law will be fulfilled, and wisdom is complete in the mouth of the faithful.

**34:9** A well-traveled man knows many things, and a man of great experience will speak with understanding.

**34:10** One who has no experience knows few things, but the one who has traveled is full of cleverness.

**34:11** I have seen many things in my travels and I understand more than I can express.

**34:12** Many times I was in danger of death, but I was saved through these experiences.

**34:13** The spirit of those who fear the Lord shall live, for their hope is in him who saves them.

**34:14** Whoever fears the Lord is not afraid and will not be a coward, for he is his hope.

**34:15** Blessed is the soul of the man who fears the Lord! To whom does he look, and who is his support?

**34:16** The eyes of the Lord are upon those who love him, a mighty shield and a strong support, a shelter from the burning wind and a shade from the noonday sun, a guard against stumbling and a help against falling.

**34:17** He lifts up the soul and makes the eyes shine; he gives healing, life, and blessing.

**34:18** If one sacrifices from what has been wrongly obtained, the offering is blemished, and the scoffing of the lawless is not acceptable.

**34:19** The Most High has no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly, nor is he propitiated for sins by a multitude of sacrifices.

**34:20** Like one who kills a son before his father's eyes is the man who brings a sacrifice from the property of the poor.

**34:21** The bread of the needy is the life of the poor; whoever deprives them of it is a man of blood.

**34:22** He who takes away a neighbor's living murders him, and whoever deprives a hired laborer of his wages sheds blood.

**34:23** When one builds and another tears down, what do they gain but labor?

**34:24** When one prays and another curses, to whose voice will the Lord listen?

**34:25** If a man washes after touching a corpse, and touches it again, what has he gained by his washing?

**34:26** So if a man fasts for his sins, and goes again and does the same thing, who will listen to his prayer, and what has he gained by his humiliation?
